prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat bands at magic twist angles and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene, opening moire quantum matter.

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is the one candidate that all eight of us placed on our ballots, and the breadth of agreement tracks real substance. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model made a sharp, quantitative prediction (flat bands at a magic angle) from a simple starting point, and the 2018 experiments showed correlated insulators and superconductivity in a tunable carbon-only system. It created a platform where interaction strength is set by twist angle and gating, which has produced many follow-on phenomena in moire systems. The prediction-then-experiment structure gives a clean two-sided prize with three credited names. As someone who works on statistical physics of many-interacting-degree-of-freedom systems, I value that this opens a controllable arena for strongly correlated matter rather than one more material. I moved this above my own opening first choice (B003) as my preferred configuration because the case for it is stronger when judged on breadth of support and on how well attribution fits the credited names.
statement.case_against: The origin of the superconductivity and the nature of the correlated states remain unsettled, so the interpretation of the headline phase is not closed and the recognition could be judged early. The boundary between the founding discovery and later moire work (fractional Chern insulators, other moire families) is not sharp, and several experimental contributors, including the first-author team of the 2018 papers and groups working on related moire systems, fall outside any three-name allocation. A prize now might also fix a narrative the field is still revising.

responses.point: Kroll ranks optical lattice clocks (B022, Katori and Ye) first, arguing that the magic-wavelength lattice removes Doppler and recoil shifts, that 10^-18 uncertainty has been independently reproduced, and that this is squarely in the tradition of measurement-driven prizes.
responses.response: I accept the maturity and attribution argument: the two-person configuration is cleaner than ours for B028, and the independent confirmation across several laboratories is stronger than for twisted bilayer graphene. I ranked it lower (7th) only because the scientific novelty beyond the measurement-precision frontier seems narrower to me, and I am an outsider to precision metrology, so I defer partly to Kroll and Lindroth on its significance. I do not think the unsettled superconductivity in B028 is disqualifying, because the prize would reward the prediction and discovery of the platform, not the pairing mechanism. I keep B022 as an alternative, and I would not object strongly if the committee preferred it.

responses.point: Lindroth also puts B022 first and calls the Katori-Ye pairing clean, noting that the clocks open redefinition of the second, tests of fundamental constants and relativistic geodesy.
responses.response: The practical and fundamental-physics reach she describes is real. My reservation is a modest disagreement about balance: B022 is mostly a story of ever-improving accuracy, whereas B028 opened a new class of many-body phenomena. She is right that the clean credit makes B022 safer on attribution, and I accept that this is a genuine advantage over B028, where Cao and other experimentalists are left out. I do not claim that breadth of ballot support settles this.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks the Higgs experimental discovery (B037; Della Negra, Jenni, Virdee) first, as the completion of the experimental basis of the electroweak sector, with theory already honoured in 2013.
responses.response: I agree that the discovery is of the first rank and fully mature. My disagreement is about attribution: a trio of detector conceivers stands in for two collaborations of thousands, and Danielsson himself acknowledges that the 2012 analysis leadership is a different group. That is a more serious allocation problem than the Cao and Dean questions in B028, so I would not choose B037 unless the committee finds a defensible framing around the conception and construction of the detectors. Only four of eight members ranked it, and two of them placed it seventh or eighth.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks dynamical mean-field theory (B018) first for its non-perturbative treatment of the Mott transition and its link to electronic-structure calculations, and ranks twisted bilayer graphene second, noting that credit is not entirely clean because the Cao team and other groups contributed.
responses.response: We agree that B028 is close to the correlated-electron questions in his own field, and his caution about attribution is one I share. I think the experimental credit to Jarillo-Herrero as group leader is defensible within the supplied names. I see B018 as a major methodological advance but the support behind it is just one first-place vote, so I do not see a basis for making it the preferred configuration.

responses.point: Olsson ranks LaAlO3/SrTiO3 oxide interfaces (B001) first, and B028 second, saying the TBG credit is a natural theory-plus-experiment pairing even though first-author experimentalists are not creditable.
responses.response: I agree with her reading of the credit structure and her flag on early timing. I place B001 lower: it is a well-defined discovery, but its mechanism (oxygen vacancies and intermixing versus electronic reconstruction) is still debated, which makes maturity at least as questionable as for B028. That is a counterpoint to a first-place ranking that rests on a different maturity standard than the one used against twisted bilayer graphene.

uncertainties: Whether the unresolved origin of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene makes recognition premature or whether the platform discovery alone suffices
Whether three names (including the choice of Bistritzer) is the right allocation when the first-author experimental team and other moire groups are excluded

Whether the committee regards B003 (cavity method and message passing) as physics rather than computer science, and how it relates to the earlier Parisi recognition, which I cannot resolve from the supplied text
How the committee weighs closeness to the 2025 superconducting-circuit prize against B014 and the 2024 machine-learning prize against B003
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. My interdisciplinary and neural-network work is adjacent to B003 (statistical physics of computation and learning), which I flag as an intellectual closeness, not a personal or institutional connection; I do not see any documented tie to the credited names of B003, B028 or B022.
